evidence.quote: | Ok [ "borrow"; m; c ] -> UseCases.borrow ports m c |> render showBorrow

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The block rule is decided in Tier 2. Accounts.isBlocked, ensureNotBlocked and standing are applied in Loans.borrow, Loans.renew and Holds.place. Tier 3 (Views.members, Views.standing) only calls Accounts.isBlocked and Accounts.standing. The CLI only branches on the Tier 3 view flag v.Blocked / m.Blocked to choose its text. The change also removes the existing CLI-side fines-minus-payments >= 5.00m check, so the rule now lives only in Tier 2.

evidence.quote: | Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added below Tier 4. The new renew and standing use cases reach the store and clock through the existing commit/query helpers over Ports. The change removes the earlier direct ports.Store.Load/Save and ports.Clock() calls in the CLI, and the CLI's direct call to Loans.renew (Tier 4 calling into Tier 2).

evidence.quote: blocked until it is below {money Policy.blockingBalance}
let isBlocked memberId (library: Library) = owed memberId library >= Policy.blockingBalance

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The blocking balance has one definition, Policy.blockingBalance, and every use references it, including the refusal message. What a member owes comes from Accounts.owed, and the blocked status comes from Accounts.isBlocked. The CLI's copied 5.00m literal and its own owed calculation are removed.

evidence.quote: blocked until it is below {money threshold}

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The per-member-type threshold and the block decision both live in Tier 2 (Policy, Accounts). The refusal now carries the threshold Tier 2 decided inside the MemberBlocked error, so Tier 3 only formats it and does not look up a balance itself.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Only pure Tier 1/2 code changes (Model, Policy, Accounts) plus formatting in Views. No new effect, no port bypass, and no Tier 4 call into Tier 2.

evidence.quote: | Some threshold -> owed memberId library >= threshold
| Some threshold when owed memberId library >= threshold ->

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The thresholds have one definition, Policy.blockingBalance by member type, used through blockingBalanceOf. But the change copies the blocked predicate (owed >= threshold, None means not blocked). In change set 1, ensureNotBlocked called isBlocked; now it re-implements the predicate instead. The two copies agree today, but they are separate definitions of the same status.
